NLT.1:
“Come, let us return to the LORD.
He has torn us to pieces;
now he will heal us.
He has injured us;
now he will bandage our wounds.
NLT.2:
In just a short time he will restore us,
so that we may live in his presence.
NLT.3:
Oh, that we might know the LORD!
Let us press on to know him.
He will respond to us as surely as the arrival of dawn
or the coming of rains in early spring.”
NLT.4:
“O Israel and Judah,
what should I do with you?” asks the LORD.
“For your love vanishes like the morning mist
and disappears like dew in the sunlight.
NLT.5:
I sent my prophets to cut you to pieces —
to slaughter you with my words,
with judgments as inescapable as light.
NLT.6:
I want you to show love,
not offer sacrifices.
I want you to know me
more than I want burnt offerings.
NLT.7:
But like Adam, you broke my covenant
and betrayed my trust.
NLT.8:
“Gilead is a city of sinners,
tracked with footprints of blood.
NLT.9:
Priests form bands of robbers,
waiting in ambush for their victims.
They murder travelers along the road to Shechem
and practice every kind of sin.
NLT.10:
Yes, I have seen something horrible in Ephraim and Israel:
My people are defiled by prostituting themselves with other gods!
NLT.11:
“O Judah, a harvest of punishment is also waiting for you,
though I wanted to restore the fortunes of my people.

AMP.1:
"Come and let us return [in repentance] to the LORD,
For He has torn us, but He will heal us;
He has wounded us, but He will bandage us.
AMP.2:
"After two days He will revive us;
On the third day He will raise us up
That we may live before Him.
AMP.3:
"So let us know and become personally acquainted with Him; let us press on to know and understand fully the [greatness of the] LORD [to honor, heed, and deeply cherish Him].
His appearing is prepared and is as certain as the dawn,
And He will come to us [in salvation] like the [heavy] rain,
Like the spring rain watering the earth."
AMP.4:
O Ephraim, what shall I do with you?
O Judah, what shall I do with you?
For your [wavering] loyalty and kindness are [transient] like the morning cloud
And like the dew that goes away early.
AMP.5:
Therefore, I have hewn them in pieces by [the words of] the prophets;
I have slain them by the words of My mouth;
My judgments [pronounced upon them by the prophets] are like the light that shines forth [obvious to all].
AMP.6:
For I desire and delight in [steadfast] loyalty [faithfulness in the covenant relationship], rather than sacrifice,
And in the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
AMP.7:
But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant;
There they have dealt treacherously against Me.
AMP.8:
Gilead is a city of wrongdoers;
It is tracked with bloody footprints.
AMP.9:
And as bands of robbers [lie in] wait for a man,
So a band of priests murder on the road toward Shechem [covering their crimes in that city of refuge];
Certainly they have committed crimes and outrages.
AMP.10:
I have seen a horrible thing [sins of every kind] in the house of Israel!
Ephraim's prostitution (idolatry) is there; Israel has defiled itself.
AMP.11:
Also, O Judah, there is a harvest [of divine judgment] appointed for you,
When I restore the fortunes of My people [who have been slaves to the misery of sin].

MSG.1:
"Come on, let's go back to God.
He hurt us, but he'll heal us.
He hit us hard,
but he'll put us right again.
MSG.2:
In a couple of days we'll feel better.
By the third day he'll have made us brand-new,
Alive and on our feet,
fit to face him.
MSG.3:
We're ready to study God,
eager for God-knowledge.
As sure as dawn breaks,
so sure is his daily arrival.
He comes as rain comes,
as spring rain refreshing the ground."
MSG.4:
"What am I to do with you, Ephraim?
What do I make of you, Judah?
Your declarations of love last no longer
than morning mist and predawn dew.
MSG.5:
That's why I use prophets to shake you to attention,
why my words cut you to the quick:
To wake you up to my judgment
blazing like light.
MSG.6:
I'm after love that lasts, not more religion.
I want you to know God, not go to more prayer meetings.
MSG.7:
You broke the covenant—just like Adam!
You broke faith with me—ungrateful wretches!
MSG.8:
"Gilead has become Crime City—
blood on the sidewalks, blood on the streets.
MSG.9:
It used to be robbers who mugged pedestrians.
Now it's gangs of priests
Assaulting worshipers on their way to Shechem.
Nothing is sacred to them.
MSG.10:
"I saw a shocking thing in the country of Israel:
Ephraim worshiping in a religious whorehouse,
and Israel in the mud right there with him.
MSG.11:
"You're as bad as the worst of them, Judah.
You've been sowing wild oats. Now it's harvest time.
